arrival.note: NOT AN ARRIVAL, A BOUND. Nothing dates a hypothesised household, and a year would be a claim nobody made. `not_later_than` the scene date states the only thing the inference carries: the town's need is measured on 1 July 1835, so the household is posited as being here by then and at no stated time before it.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not claimed. The layer infers households, not families: the person entries here are the ones the trade argument requires and nothing counts wives or children, because counting them would multiply a hypothesis by an invention.

origin.note: Not claimed. Where a hypothesised resident came from is unknowable by construction, and the documented layer's origins (Vermont, Washington, Ann Arbor) are evidence about those men and not a distribution to sample from.

reason_for_coming.note: Not claimed for the person. The reason the HOUSEHOLD is in the dataset is the trade argument in research_note, which is a statement about the town and not about a motive.

lives_at.note: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_north_d5_026 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

works_at.note: recon_1835_north_c1_020 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. The workplace is assigned from the reconstruction schedule's workshop and store families for this trade.

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the scene date IS the hypothesis: this household exists in the dataset because the town of 1 July 1835 demonstrably needed households of this trade. It is not a finding about anybody's whereabouts.

occupation.note: A TOWN PACKING THOUSANDS OF HOGS A SEASON NEEDS COOPERS, AND THIS DATASET HELD NONE. Andreas records that Clybourne packed some 250 head of cattle and about 2,000 hogs in the season of 1833, that George W. Dole packed a further 250 cattle and 1,000 hogs at the same place, and that the Newberry & Dole house on the South Branch packed 300 cattle and 1,400 hogs in 1834 (scan p. 1151). Packed provisions travel in barrels and barrels are made by coopers. The documented layer holds a packer, two slaughter-houses and not one cooper. Four cooper households are inferred against the schedule's six W3 cooper, wagon or wheelwright shops.

name_basis.note: THE NAME IS INVENTED. No source names this resident, and this field is not a finding about anybody — it is a label so that a reconstructed household reads as a household rather than as a row in a table. It was drawn from the New England and New York pool in data/reconstruction/1835_invented_name_pools.json, which is seeded from the names of the 76 ATTESTED residents this project holds — real people, named from cited sources — so that an invented resident is named the way this town's documented residents were actually named rather than the way a story would name one. The community was drawn WITHOUT a weighting that any source supports. The proportions of the documented layer, which is overwhelmingly New England and New York with an older French colonial presence and a small Irish one. Applied to every trade for which no source speaks to who did the work. The evidence for the pool itself: The dominant documented group in this dataset by a wide margin. Attested origins among the named residents include Vermont (three households), Washington County Vermont, Burlington, Connecticut by way of Detroit, Sackett's Harbor New York, Guilford Vermont, and 'New England'. Attested surnames of this stock in the town include Harmon, Taylor, Brown, Davis, Porter, Wright, Blodgett, Carpenter, Carver, Caton, Calhoun, Peck, Dole, Newberry and Bates.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - fourth of 4 cooper households in this layer, in the north division. A TOWN PACKING THOUSANDS OF HOGS A SEASON NEEDS COOPERS, AND THIS DATASET HELD NONE. Andreas records that Clybourne packed some 250 head of cattle and about 2,000 hogs in the season of 1833, that George W. Dole packed a further 250 cattle and 1,000 hogs at the same place, and that the Newberry & Dole house on the South Branch packed 300 cattle and 1,400 hogs in 1834 (scan p. 1151). Packed provisions travel in barrels and barrels are made by coopers. The documented layer holds a packer, two slaughter-houses and not one cooper. Four cooper households are inferred against the schedule's six W3 cooper, wagon or wheelwright shops. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
